MullerSong1997 and Tuvaandorj2020 address localization of directly observed regression discontinuities, not connected honest fuzzy-RD LATE intervals with a weak denominator.
PorterYu2015 handles fixed-jump unknown-cutoff oracle substitution and NoackRothe2024 handles weak fuzzy-RD inference at a known cutoff; neither covers the joint vanishing-jump regime.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves honesty of bias-aware Anderson–Rubin confidence sets for fuzzy RD under observed-regression smoothness and permits weak identification; it does not study an unknown cutoff.

Theorem 4 gives n-consistent unknown-cutoff estimation with a nonstandard argmax limit under the paper's fixed-jump sharp-RD setting, and Theorem 5 gives oracle treatment-effect inference after cutoff estimation.
The paper derives optimal confidence intervals and sharp efficiency bounds for linear functionals over convex regression classes, including RD applications.
The paper studies smooth-regression change-point localization, obtains n⁻¹ localization for a fixed jump, and derives a two-sided Brownian limit with triangular drift under shrinking jumps.

The paper establishes unknown-threshold RD/white-noise correspondence and minimax location rates for discontinuities in derivatives; it does not state a fuzzy-RD connected-LATE interval-length frontier.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives lower bounds and near-minimax localization for multivariate distributional change points with unrestricted vector signals, rather than a latent monotone fuzzy-RD causal class.
LoTTA is a Bayesian RD method incorporating uncertainty about an unknown cutoff; the available paper does not claim a frequentist honest minimax connected-interval frontier.

source_verification_receipts.version: KEO Discussion Paper 200, April 2026, unpublished working paper
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The public working-paper text discusses fuzzy RD and unknown discontinuity points in separate extension sections. It has no theorem for their joint weak-cutoff minimax problem; its unpublished status is disclosed and is not used for an N-flag.

The paper gives valid inference after data-dependent target selection in norm-maximization problems including threshold and break models, but does not analyze weak fuzzy-RD ratios or minimax connected-interval length.
This is the standard fuzzy-RD identification source for interpreting the reduced-form Wald ratio as a local complier effect under continuity, exclusion, and monotonicity.
